endorsements.quote: The Data Card initiative can be a major part of this assessment, as it necessitates the reporting of dataset features, including its origins, the populations represented, and its priorprocessing[13].

Before performing any data processing or modeling, we first recommend that AIresearchersassesstheir training and testing datasets and consider the ways in which they may be under-counting certain populations including through previous application of exclusion criteria to the dataset.

unlisted_practices: AI researchers should add a participant flow diagram to AI studies that tracks the number and sociodemographic and clinical characteristics of participants excluded at each study phase (recruitment, exclusion criteria, input-level exclusion, outcome-level exclusion).

AI researchers should report standardized mean differences between successive steps of the participant flow diagram, treating an absolute SMD greater than 0.1 as a meaningful change in sample composition.
AI researchers should think critically about which sociodemographic and clinical factors are relevant to track in their study, rather than passively reporting.
AI researchers should seek to identify why disparities in study exclusion, treatment access, and follow-up occur and how they can be prevented.
AI researchers should report, as a key limitation or adjust study design for greater inclusion, when the participant flow diagram shows disproportionate exclusion of demographic groups.
AI researchers should not extrapolate clinical algorithm results to populations excluded from the study sample.

screen.reason: This is a framework/recommendation paper advocating for participant flow diagrams detailing excluded demographic characteristics to promote health equity and bias mitigation in health AI research.
